answer.label: Not traced to Terry Pratchett — an unsourced attribution
answer.authorDates: Unsourced wording, listed on Wikiquote by September 2005
answer.sourceLine: No Pratchett source has been found for this line. It was added to Wikiquote’s Pratchett page without a source in 2005 and moved to the talk page’s “Unsourced” list in 2009. It reworks an anonymous saying: “Good judgment comes from experience, and experience comes from bad judgment.”

source.trailTitle: How the attribution can be traced
trail: Wikiquote, 19 September 2005: the line is added to the Terry Pratchett page under “Attributed,” with no source — 2005 revision ↗
Wikiquote, 26 January 2009: an editor moves unsourced quotes, this one among them, to the talk page’s “Unsourced” list, where it still is — 2009 revision ↗
Quote Investigator traces the older saying “Good judgment comes from experience…” to an anonymous 1932 newspaper item. Its article does not mention Pratchett — Quote Investigator ↗
A search of the L-Space Pratchett Quote File, a large fan collection of lines from his books and Usenet posts, finds no match — Pratchett Quote File ↗
source.excerptNote: As it appeared, with no source, in the 19 September 2005 revision of Wikiquote’s Terry Pratchett page. The same wording now sits on the “Unsourced” list of that page’s talk page.
source.rightsNote: No published work by Terry Pratchett is known to contain this wording, so there is no work whose copyright status could be stated. His novels are in copyright, but this line has not been traced to any of them, and the wording has no identified author.

author.name: Anonymous
author.heading: About Anonymous
author.metaLine: Folk saying · in print by 1932 (Quote Investigator)
author.bio: The idea behind this line is an anonymous saying: good judgment comes from experience, and experience comes from bad judgment. Quote Investigator’s earliest match is a 1932 Indiana newspaper item, where the speaker did not claim to have coined it. Later credits to Will Rogers are unsupported, and Rita Mae Brown used it in 2001 as an “old saying.” The “lack of wisdom” version credited to Terry Pratchett has no identified author.

misattribution.heading: Why it gets pinned on Pratchett
misattribution.intro: Clever, unsourced lines often end up credited to Terry Pratchett, and Quote Investigator ↗ has looked into several of them. This one has no Pratchett source that anyone has found.

items.why: Wikiquote requires a precise source for every quotation and lists this line as unsourced on its Pratchett talk page ↗. It is not among the sourced quotations on his main Wikiquote page ↗.

items.who: J. L. Collins, The Simple Path to Wealth
items.why: Goodreads ↗ files the line under Collins’s personal-finance book, where it is printed with a “—Terry Pratchett” credit. When a book quotes an attribution, it repeats the credit. It is not a source for it.

The line has the same shape as “Good judgment comes from experience, and experience comes from bad judgment.” Quote Investigator ↗ finds that saying in 1932 and says the link to Will Rogers is unsupported. Rita Mae Brown called it an “old saying” when she used it.

misattribution.truthLine: No Pratchett source has been found. Treat the line as an unsourced attribution that reworks an anonymous saying. See Wikiquote’s Unsourced list ↗.

context.heading: An old joke in new words
lead: The line is a short version of a joke about experience that was already circulating. Quote Investigator ↗ found its earliest match in The Muncie Evening Press in 1932. There, Fred Rose was reported quoting: “Good Judgment depends mostly on experience and experience usually comes from poor judgment.”

The same article notes a related thought from Oscar Wilde, in Lady Windermere’s Fan (published 1893): “Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.” The “lack of wisdom” wording gives the same circular joke a new vocabulary. A famous name is what made it travel.
